court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: I Additional District and Sessions Judge (PCR), Thanjavur - O.S.No.20 of 2009
case_name: Annapottu Ammal (Died) vs Tamilmani on 14 November, 2025
facts_of_case: The first defendant in a suit for partition has preferred the present appeal challenging the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

legal_principles.principle: A person who is not entitled to seek partition of residential houses cannot pray for dismissal of the suit.
legal_principles.held: The plaintiffs are not entitled to seek partition of residential houses since they are residing separately. Hence, they prayed for dismissal of the suit.

legal_principles.principle: A person who has not received any share from the suit property is not entitled to seek partition.
legal_principles.held: The plaintiffs have never received any share from the suit schedule property. Therefore, proper Court fee has not been paid.

legal_principles.principle: A person who is the legally wedded wife of a deceased person is entitled to receive a share in the ancestral properties.
legal_principles.held: The marriage of Duraisamy Udaiyar with 7th defendant has been held prior to 1949. In such circumstances, the 7th defendant is the legally wedded wife of the deceased Duraisamy Udaiyar.

legal_principles.principle: A person who has purchased a property from the income of family properties is not entitled to claim absolute ownership.
legal_principles.held: Item Nos. 94 to 104 were purchased by Duraisamy Udaiyar from the income of the family properties in the name of 2nd defendant and therefore, it is not the absolute properties of the 2nd defendant.

outcome.final_order: Modified shares of all parties as per points raised in grounds.

use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu law and family settlements
representing clients in joint family disputes
